clue.text: Nick, American talks nonsense on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: in American slang to gum is to chatter idly or talk nonsense

explanation.surface: An American called Nick, thinking it over, realises he talks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang verbs for steal, the second an old thieves' cant term.

clue.text: Mike in bed succeeded getting hearty kisses

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the letter goes within the bed word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
Mike is the radio code word for M
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone called Mike, having got into bed, wins some enthusiastic kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a loud kiss given with a hearty smacking of the lips.

clue.text: Main theatre play about old man perhaps

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The leading theatre stages a play about an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: An old man is Australian slang for a fully grown male kangaroo, hence 'perhaps': it is one example of a marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: Metatherians are the marsupial mammals, and the old man kangaroo is one such animal.

clue.text: Work on familiar flower for Edmund

parts.note: a machine that works goes
old as in a familiar, long-known friend or haunt

explanation.surface: Someone named Edmund is told to tend a familiar bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund is Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet whose archaic spellings Chambers records; in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser's spelling this word means the marigold, a garden flower, as well as gold.

clue.text: City arrest brings elation

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
stasis is an arrest or stoppage of growth or flow

explanation.surface: An arrest in the City of London brings delight to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old form of ecstasy, a state of rapturous joy.

clue.text: Dash out of bounds, demurely somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters fit together in some other way
the bounds of a word are its two ends, and these are put out

parts.note: the word taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone darts off where they shouldn't, in an oddly demure manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the D and Y at the ends of demurely, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the printer's long dash, the width of a letter M, used for parenthesis.

clue.text: Cut calls with contemptuous looks

parts.note: a dialect word for cut or lop, recorded in Chambers
rings as in telephone calls

explanation.surface: Someone cuts their phone calls short while giving scornful glances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneerings are scornful expressions, curled-lip looks of disdain.

clue.text: Revolving index, one left on island — dash!

parts.note: a means one
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the abbreviation for island
dad is a dialect verb meaning to dash or strike violently

explanation.surface: Someone stranded alone on an island exclaims in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'dash!' is really the Scots verb, not a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alidad is the rotating sighting arm with pointer on a surveying instrument such as a theodolite.

clue.text: Leaders in Sun introduce mean comment in the margin

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their heads, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
to denote is to mean or signify

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor tells staff to insert a nasty remark in the paper's margin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun reads as the newspaper, which fits a margin comment, but it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A note written beside the main text is a marginal annotation.

clue.text: Motion enters race for an English poet

indicators.note: motion is movement, and the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the word taken as written

explanation.surface: A proposal is tabled at a meeting before a contest in honour of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The English poet is Spenser, who used this spelling; 'race' is lineage, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spenser's spelling the word is strain, meaning lineage or stock, a sense of race.

clue.text: Guys love small white fish from Canada

parts.note: guys are men
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
mini means small

explanation.surface: Some men are fond of a little pale fish caught in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the round whitefish of North American lakes, named after a Native American people.

clue.text: Stop second entry before revised date agreed

parts.note: ho is an old call to stop or halt

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
an entry as in a ship's log
the word taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone halts a second record of a meeting until the changed date is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To homologate is to confirm or ratify formally, so the past form means approved.

clue.text: Passage about say, Manila Bay island

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a corridor is a passage
e.g., for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A narrow sea passage near an island in Manila Bay is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Corregidor is the fortified island at the entrance to Manila Bay in the Philippines, famous from the Second World War.

clue.text: Ring employers right away for soft tissues

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: users employ things
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A job seeker is told to phone employers straight away about soft jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a callus is the soft tissue that forms over a cut surface of a plant.

clue.text: Unique Close for limited accommodation

parts.note: single means sole or unique
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A one-off cul-de-sac is chosen for a small housing scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A Close is a British name for a residential cul-de-sac, which makes the surface about housing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a single-end is a one-room flat, accommodation of very restricted size.

clue.text: Display set up in US plant for flyers

indicators.note: placed in the plant name means it goes inside those letters

parts.note: camas is a North American plant of the lily family with edible bulbs

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: to air views is to display them

explanation.surface: A floral display is built inside an American plant nursery for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Cariamas, or seriemas, are long-legged South American birds, so creatures that fly.

clue.text: French opera with female replacing male in short cape

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: Manon is Massenet's French opera
F is the abbreviation for female
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A French opera production casts a woman in a male role wearing a little cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanon is the short cape worn by the Pope over the shoulders at solemn Mass.

clue.text: Upset fish in tin

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy to find their fish comes canned.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaken describes someone disturbed or emotionally rattled, the same as upset.

clue.text: Stuff found in wee oldie working outside close to Aberdeen

indicators.note: outside means wrapped round the other piece
working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the word taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the city name

explanation.surface: Something is found in a little old person working away near Aberdeen, where wee means small.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'wee' is the Scots word for small, fitting Aberdeen; in the definition it is urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Indole is an organic compound found in faeces and urine, giving the smell of excrement.

clue.text: Eastern bosun using second compass back to front

indicators.note: the back letter is moved to the front, so the word rotates by one place

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
compass as in scope or range

explanation.surface: A ship's officer in the East steers by a spare compass mounted the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A serang is the boatswain or skipper of a crew of lascars in South Asian waters.

clue.text: US department store's taken up surrounding parking for surveillance device

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means lifted so the word reads from bottom to top
surrounding means placed around another piece

parts.note: Macy's is the New York department store
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: An American store's car park is watched over by a security camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A spycam is a small concealed camera used to watch people secretly.

clue.text: Water plant is surrounded by essence

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: alma is soul, the essence of a being
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aquatic plant is steeped in a fragrant extract.
explanation.definitionFit: Alisma is the water plantain genus, plants of ponds and marshes.

clue.text: Quiet for minute in Greek province leads to poem over there

indicators.note: one thing for another means it stands in its place

parts.note: st! is a call for hush
m is the abbreviation for minute
a nomos is a province or department of Greece

explanation.surface: Silence for a minute in a Greek region prompts verse from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over there' means in Greece: the answer is a Greek word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostos is a Greek poem about a hero's homecoming, such as the Odyssey.

clue.text: Very large victim for fish-eating bird

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
prey is a victim

explanation.surface: A very large victim is caught by a hunting bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a raptor that lives by diving for fish.

clue.text: Lecherous female posed with younger adult

parts.note: sat as an artist's model sits or poses
yr is the abbreviation for younger
A is the film rating for adult

explanation.surface: A predatory woman models alongside a young grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyra is a female satyr, and satyrs are lustful creatures of myth.

clue.text: Doctor about right to get pellet

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: pill is slang for a doctor, recorded in Chambers
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to be accurate about handing out a tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: A prill is a small round granule, such as fertiliser formed into beads.

clue.text: Look at entry to Sainsbury's for lunchbox

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
at and in both mean present at a place

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its first letter, the way in

parts.note: the opening letter of the shop name

explanation.surface: Someone checks the entrance of a supermarket for a lunch container.
explanation.walkthrough: Sainsbury's is a British supermarket chain; lunchbox is British slang for a man's genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunchbox is slang for the male genitals, which the loins delicately denote.

clue.text: Discern disrupting end, hard going for tyrant's territory

indicators.note: disrupting means breaking into another piece
going means leaving, so that letter departs

parts.note: death is the end
H is hard on pencils
to spot is to discern

explanation.surface: Seeing a dictator's realm collapse brings a difficult ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotat is a territory ruled by a despot, such as a Byzantine despotate.

clue.text: Accountant with mobile on street, oddly scary and perverse

parts.note: CA is a Chartered Accountant
M is an abbreviation for mobile
St is the abbreviation for street
eerie means oddly scary, weird and frightening

explanation.surface: An accountant on the street with a phone looks odd and frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an instruction to take odd letters, but here it is part of the description eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Camsteerie is a Scots word meaning unruly or contrary, which is perverse behaviour.

clue.text: Bury around goal get weaker as before

indicators.note: around means wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: to inter is to bury
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Burying someone near the goalposts leaves you feeling feebler.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic verb means to make or become tender, that is to soften or weaken.

clue.text: One boring female endlessly formal, hating men

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the first piece goes inside
without its end the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Miss is the title for an unmarried female
an means one
dry as in stiff, coolly formal

explanation.surface: A tedious, stiff woman is said to dislike men.
explanation.definitionFit: Misandry is hatred of men, the counterpart of misogyny.

clue.text: Source of herbs mentioned, Australian to the end

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of its place and sent to the end

parts.note: said means mentioned
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian names where herbs come from, at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sida is a plant genus of the mallow family that includes many herbs.
